content: Ligand 1 is the methyl ester probe, whose cap cyclopropane CH is atom 18, bonded to the carbonyl at atom 16. The aryl result reframed this run and I am spending the rest of it mapping which flat ring at C4 keeps the 0.70 activity while costing least in drug-likeness. A plain benzene gave the activity and ruined QED at LogP 5; the variants in flight replace it with pyridine, pyrimidine and methylpyrazole. This one takes it furthest: a 1-methylimidazol-4-yl is the most polar aromatic I can put there, roughly two and a half log units below benzene, while adding no hydrogen-bond donor of its own - which matters, because the methylamino substituent showed how expensive an extra donor is on this scaffold. At about 333 Da with LogP near 2.6 it should post the best QED of the aryl series by some margin. The open question is whether that much nitrogen in the ring is still read as the same flat aromatic feature, or whether the electron density has shifted too far.
